_lakes_note: One block per lake. With more than one block a run must name its lake: pass --lake <name>. Each block carries the lake's identity (lake_bbox / lake_key / reanalysis_lake, used to cut the ICON area when fitting perturbations), the observation series it assimilates, and the sigma_obs fitted ON that series. A lake naming no sigma_obs falls back to the top-level sigma_default. Refit sigma whenever obs_file changes: python notebooks/generate_sigma.py --lakes <name> prints the pair to paste, and writes observations/<name>/sigma_obs.json, which nothing reads at run time. The perturbation calibration lives in perturbations/<name>.json: python notebooks/generate_perturbation.py args/run_enkf.json --lake <name> [--icon].
_sigma_obs_operator_note: These sigma_obs were fitted against T_out.dat, which Simstrat writes by interpolating onto the z_out depths -- i.e. they assume "obs_operator": "linear". That operator is not on this branch yet, so until it lands a run uses nearest-cell snapping and carries a 0.25 m discretisation error these numbers do not, leaving sigma under-stated and the filter over-trusting the observations.

aegeri._sigma_obs_note: The one lake NOT on the seasonal value, kept as a plain scalar so the exception is visible here rather than hidden in two dict keys. Seasonal breaks it: pooled NIS 1.70 against 0.94 annual, stratified deep band 6.77. See local/analyses&plans/final_simple.md.
